title: Antenna length rules
idea: Shorter means higher resonant frequency. A coil makes an antenna electrically longer. Shrinking an antenna below full size costs efficiency, and a longer 5/8-wave whip gives more gain.

items: Electrically lengthening by inserting inductors in the radiating elements
Low efficiency compared to a full-sized quarter wave

config.heading: Change the antenna
config.lead: Pick a change to see what it does.

situations.label: Shorten a dipole
situations.title: Resonant frequency goes up
situations.text: Shortening a dipole increases its resonant frequency. Lengthening it, coils in series with the wires, or capacitive loading at the ends don't.

situations.label: Insert a coil in the radiating element
situations.title: Loading: electrically longer
situations.text: Antenna loading means electrically lengthening the antenna by inserting inductors in its radiating elements. Not a resistor and not a spring.

situations.label: Use the short flexible antenna on a handheld
situations.title: Low efficiency
situations.text: Compared to a full-sized quarter-wave antenna, a handheld's short flexible antenna has low efficiency.

situations.label: Put a 19-inch vertical on 2 meters
situations.title: A resonant quarter wave
situations.text: On 2 meters, 19 inches is a resonant quarter wave. That's why it's so common, not for high gain.

situations.label: Swap a 1/4-wave mobile whip for a 5/8-wave
situations.title: More gain
situations.text: For VHF or UHF mobile, a 5/8-wavelength whip has more gain than a 1/4-wave antenna.

traps.wrong: Inserting a resistor in the radiating portion of the antenna to make it resonant
traps.why: Loading uses inductors (coils) to lengthen the antenna electrically, not a resistor.

traps.wrong: It is more susceptible to receiver desensitization
traps.why: The short antenna's problem is low efficiency.
Lengthening lowers the resonant frequency. Shortening raises it.
19 inches on 2 meters is a quarter wave, not a half wave.
The 5/8-wave whip's advantage is more gain, not lower SWR.
